root_idea.summary: A settled or supporting thing at a lower surface, especially what lies beneath the foot.
root_idea.development: The root extends from a lower support to footwear and analogous lower fittings for animals, swords, and bows, then to being shod or wearing footwear and to related figurative uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested form is an inflected dual possessive of the ordinary noun نَعْلٌ, which is best presented under its singular dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: A sandal or shoe; footwear worn on the foot.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence it appears in the dual possessive construction نَعْلَيْكَ, referring to the addressee's two items of footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sole, the part of footwear that protects the foot from the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote the sole alone rather than a complete sandal or shoe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The leathern sandal or shoe of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It is attached by thongs or straps to the camel's pastern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The iron or silver shoe-like fitting at the lower end of a sword's scabbard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized use for a sword fitting analogous to footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A band of sinew or similar material fitted over the back of the curved end of a bow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This denotes a bow fitting, not footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard, rugged tract or place of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer to a barren or nearly non-growing stretch of ground.
This is a figurative or tropical Classical Arabic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lowly or despised man, figuratively one trodden underfoot like a sandal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative application to a person regarded as contemptible or submissive.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a sole or shoe onto a boot, and to shoe an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Form IV verbal use for fitting footwear or a protective sole.
These active-participial descriptions apply to a person equipped with footwear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Said of a horse marked with white at the lower pastern.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The definition concerns the characteristic white marking on the lower part of the fetlock or pastern.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Said of a wild ass with a hard hoof.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This animal use is explained by the hardness of its hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well-off or wealthy person, figuratively represented as shod.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This figurative use is contrasted with describing a poor person as barefoot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who attends to sandals or shoes at the entrance of a bath or mosque.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an occupational designation associated with caring for visitors' footwear.

cautions: The QAC lemma candidate نَعْلَي and Quranic surface نَعْلَيْكَ are normalized here to the singular citation form نَعْلٌ; the Quran occurrence itself is dual and possessive.
